messages.subject: Re: New Phylogeny Software
messages.body_plain:
Hi Arthur,

Thanks for that - very happy with the new gl2snapp() function. I've used it to create an input for SNAPP and it works well. Haven't managed to figure out snapper yet though!

Cheers,

Yael

On Friday, May 8, 2020 at 9:51:18 AM UTC+10, Arthur Georges wrote:
> Hi everyone,
>
> Hope you are all coping with the virus, the lockdowns and the mixed messages we are getting from our leaders depending on which country you are in.
>
> I would like to bring to your attention a new item of software for generating phylogenetic trees from SNP data. This has been a problematic area as many of you would know having been in heated debate with editors and reviewers. Basically,
>
> (a) Distance measures such as those offered by Phylip are contentious and out of vogue even though we now have the computational power to bootstrap them;
> (b) Generating phylogenies by concatenating sequence tags and using ML have been debunked by many, with evidence, including Adam Leache. Some editors flatly refuse to entertain these because they do not deal with the species tree, gene tree issues adequately. One said "I would rather see a phenogram!!!"
> (c) Packages like Austal II that generate trees for each sequence tag then form a consensus struggle to deal with the noise when the sequence tags are only between 20 and 69 bp, most with a single SNP.
> (d) SVD quartets deals with the species tree-gene tree issue appropriately, and has been considered by some to be the best choice, but it does not give branch lengths.
> (e) SNAPP is recommended by many, but computational limitations means that you can only include a couple of individuals per population, and so you have to toss a LOT of data.
>
> The authors of SNAPP have now developed a new package called Snapper, which overcomes the limitations of SNAPP by using, if I understand it correctly, allele profiles of populations rather than individual genotypes. So instead of trying to deal with 1035 individuals, the algorithm just has to deal with 35 populations.
>
> You might like to give it a try.
>
> Stoltz,M, Bauemer, B., Bouckaert, R., Fox, C., Hiscott, G. and Bryant, D. Bayesian inference of species trees using diffusion models. https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.07276.
>
> The software is open-source and available to download athttps://github.com/rbouckaert/snapper <http://github.com/rbouckaert/snapper>.
>
> I expect that the gl2snapp() script in dartR will produce the input file that you pass to BEAUTI to create the xlm file to then pass to Snapper, but I have not tried this.
>
> If you have the time to give this a try, post how you go against this thread, and we can make any mods to the dartR scripts as required.
>
> All the best,
>
> A
messages.body_snippet:
Hi Arthur,

Thanks for that - very happy with the new gl2snapp() function. I've used it to create an input for SNAPP and it works well. Haven't managed to figure out snapper yet though!

Cheers,

Yael

I have a fairly large genlight file with geo-referenced data, but I have about 10% missing data. When I try to use the gl.ibd function, I get this error message:

When I run a PCA, I usually deal with NA values using the tab method (like this: all_noNAs <- tab(ALL_MPB_gl, NA.method="mean").

Is there a way of dealing with the missing values here? I am fairly confident that I have the spatial coordinates inputted correctly as I modeled them off the ones in the bandicoot.gl <http://bandicoot.gl> file.

I also get a similar error when I use the by individual IBD method that is listed in the other dartR post about IBD.

messages.subject: Re: [dartR] New Beta version of dartR
messages.body_plain:
Dear Arthur
Thanks for the effort to upgrade dartR packages for SilicoDArT, the type of markers that I am using right now.
I followed the instructions, however I stuck on:
--------------------------------

install_github("green-striped-gecko/dartR", ref="dev")

Downloading GitHub repo green-striped-gecko/dartR@dev. These packages have more recent versions available. It is recommended to update all of them. Which would you like to update?
1: All
2: CRAN packages only
3: None
4: vcfR (1.10.0 -> 1.11.0) [CRAN]
---------------------------------
Trying with all of them, with no success.
Any suggestions please?

PR

El jue., 5 dic. 2019 a las 20:22, Arthur Georges (<ardy.g...@gmail.com>) escribió:

> Further to our previous announcement on the upgrade, we would like to elaborate:
>
>
> (a) dartR has been upgraded to accommodate SilicoDArT data, that is, the presence or absence of sequence tags called or not called, as well as the SNP genotype data. There are analyses that cannot be done on tag P/A data, and the scripts trap that. Both forms of data are stored as genlight objects (read in by gl.read.dart and gl.read.silicodart respectively), the distinction being whether the ploidy is 2 (SNP data) or ploidy is 1 (Tag P/A data).
>
> (b) A computational efficiency has been built in to avoid recalculating stats unnecessarily, which is embedded in the genlight objects. This may require you to run gl <- gl.compatability.check(gl) to avoid throwing errors.
>
> (c) The pcoa scripts have been substantially rewritten to distinguish between PCA (SNP or SilicoDArT data as input, covariance matrix based computations) and PCoA (distance matrix input, any distance measure pretty much). Distortions that may arise (manifested as negative eigenvalues in the noise dimensions) from using a sparse matrix (lots of NAs) or non-metric distance measures can be accommodated by applying recognised transformations (sensu ape).
>
> (d) The scripts for fixed differences have been amended to allow greater control and more diagnostics (using gl.collapse repeatedly), though gl.collapse.recursive still works.
>
> (e) A novel approach to standardizing heterozygosity across species and studies has been introduced. Not a panacea, but worth examination. Use gl.report.secondaries to estimate the number of sequence tags with no snps, and use this value in gl.report.heterozygosity (as n.invariant).
>
> There have been some bug fixes, but software development has a problem of reaching a steady state where bugs are removed but new bugs are created at the same rate. Hence the beta release.
>
> Please pipe up with issues.
>
> install.packages("leaflet.providers")
> install.packages("lifecycle")
> install.packages("farver")
> install_github("green-striped-gecko/dartR", ref="dev") # no need to upgrade prior installs, answer no.
>
> A
>

messages.subject: RE: [dartR] Error in converting gl2gi
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

The “problem” is that gl2gi is expecting diploid data in its current format.

Though I am fairly certain a gl.pcoa() should work on your data set from a genlight format, so for running a PCA there is no need to convert to genind.

Cheers, Bernd

messages.subject: gl.report.heterozygosity function not working
messages.body_plain:
Hi folks,

I'm fairly new to using the dartR package, but I'm having trouble obtaining a report on heterozygosity for the populations in my data.

I've tried running the gl.report.heterozygosity() function.
I'm using the latest version of RStudio, R v4.0.0, and have updated all packages. I was initially using the current CRAN version of dartR. The gl.report.heterozygosity() function would just hang and produce no output. Then I switched to the current development version of dartR - the function thenworked for a brief time, but now, for some reason which I cannot fathom it no longer works, but instead of hanging it gives the following error:

> x1 <- gl.report.heterozygosity(testset.gl <http://testset.gl>, +  method="pop",boxplot="standard", verbose = 5)

Starting gl.report.heterozygosity [ Build = Jacob ]
   Processing a SNP dataset
   Warning: genlight object contains monomorphic loci which will be factored into heterozygosity estimates
   Calculating Observed Heterozygosities, averaged across loci, for each population
   Calculating Expected Heterozygosities
Error in plot.new <http://plot.new>() : figure margins too large

I've tried changing plot margins [e.g. par(mar = c(0.1, 0.1, 0.1, 0.1))], but this has no effect. I also found some previous discussion on this forum about this function but this hasn't helped - I'm not sure I can install a previous version of adegenet as this apparently requires a previous version of Rtools.

Cheers,
Peter

messages.subject: Re: Adegenet 2.1.2 seppop is broken!!!
messages.body_plain:
Good news this problem has been fixed now.

Adegenet has been updated to version 2.1.3 and here seppop works on genlight objects as intended. So all the function above should now work with the latest version 2.1.3 and no need to downgrade. Version 2.1.2 is the version that should be avoided.

Cheers, Bernd

On Thursday, January 30, 2020 at 12:20:59 PM UTC+11, Bernd. Gruber wrote:
> Hi,
>
> I just noticed (actually our postdoc Russell Dinnage) that adegenet 2.1.2 has an error within the seppop function (and some dartR functions do use seppop currently, see below).
>
> Be aware gl.filter.callrate works if you do not use the method="pop". Same for some other functions.
>
>
>
> The error is nasty because Instead of a list of all population seperated it returns a list of of all the populations unchanged. Hence all the function above do not work with
>
> Adegenet 2.1.2, but do not show an error.
>
>
> We notified the adegenet guys to correct the error. Until then I advise to "downgrade" to version adegenet 2.1.1, which works as intended.
>
>
> To downgrade the easiest way is to delete the package from your library folder and type:
>
> library(devtools)
> install_version("adegenet", version = "2.1.1", repos = "http://cran.us.r-project.org")
>
>
>

Hi,
I am quite new to DartR and bioinformatics in general.
Therefore, thank you for such a comprehensive guide to this extremely useful package and for this very helpful group.

I would like to check if there is a correlation between individual heterozygosity and missing data, particularly at a specific minimum coverage (5), to see if I should increase this threshold slightly.

Is there an easy way to plot this?

Thank you in advance.

Best,
Ana

messages.subject_clean: Plot individual heterozygosity and missing data
messages.body_plain:
Hi Anna,

Try this.

# Grab the test set
  gl <- testset.gl <http://testset.gl>
# Assign each individual as a population
  pop(gl) <- indNames(gl)
# Calculate Heterozygosity
  hetro <- gl.report.heterozygosity(gl)
# Display heterozygosity
  hetro$Ho
# Calculate the call rate by individual
  ind.call.rate <- 1 - rowSums(is.na <http://is.na>(as.matrix(gl)))/nLoc(gl)
# Display call rate
  ind.call.rate
#Plot heterozygosity against call rate
  plot(x=ind.call.rate,y=hetro$Ho)
